evidence: src/domain/product.ts: Product.reserve(quantity) checks `if (quantity > this.available)` and throws new DomainError("INSUFFICIENT_STOCK", `Insufficient stock for product ${this.id}: requested ${quantity}, available ${this.available}`)

src/domain/stock-allocation-service.ts: StockAllocationService.reserve(lines) checks `if (line.quantity > product.availableQuantity)` and throws new DomainError("INSUFFICIENT_STOCK", `Insufficient stock for product ${product.id}: requested ${line.quantity}, available ${product.availableQuantity}`), the same check and message
src/domain/stock-allocation-service.ts: the service reads Product's availableQuantity getter to re-evaluate the rule instead of asking Product whether a reservation is allowed
src/domain/order-status.ts: transition rules (nextFulfilmentStatus, isCancellable) are defined only here and reused by Order.advanceTo/cancel, so this part of the module keeps its rules in one place
parsedVerdict.reasoning:
The module covers one concern: order placement and stock allocation. That concern is split into an Order aggregate (order.ts, order-line.ts, order-status.ts), a Product aggregate (product.ts), repository ports and a stock allocation domain service. Every file reports failures through DomainError. Order-status rules live only in order-status.ts, and line validation lives only in OrderLine.

However, the stock-sufficiency invariant is duplicated. Product.reserve owns the rule 'quantity must not exceed available' and throws DomainError('INSUFFICIENT_STOCK', ...). StockAllocationService.reserve copies the same comparison against product.availableQuantity and builds the identical error and message itself. It does this so that a multi-line reservation is all-or-nothing. Because the service re-implements the check through a getter instead of asking Product (for example, through a canReserve method), the rule now lives in two places and the two copies can drift apart. The rubric names this kind of duplication as a failure.

violations.message: StockAllocationService.reserve copies the insufficient-stock invariant from Product.reserve: the same `quantity > available` comparison, the same INSUFFICIENT_STOCK code and the same message. It works around the Product abstraction by reading availableQuantity. Move the check into Product (for example, a canReserve method) and have the service call it, so the rule lives in one place.
